another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, there are some specific rules that apply. To continue receiving Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over, they usually need to be in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course at a school, college, or similar institution

Or has he recently left education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually left education recently, but he's signed up with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that helpful information.

That's good news regarding eligibility. When a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, Child Benefit can potentially continue for 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service (or the armed services).

Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to make sure everything is in order:

1. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

2. **Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for him. And no, he's not working - he's just been taking some time to figure things out. He's not getting any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex is 17 and registered with a careers service** – Although he's over 16 and has left education, Child Benefit can continue for up to **20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

✅ **You live in the UK** – You're based in Manchester.

✅ **Alex lives with you** – This means you're responsible for him.

✅ **No one else is claiming** – Only one person can claim Child Benefit per child, and no one else is claiming for Alex.

✅ **Alex isn't working significant hours or claiming benefits** – He's not working 24+ hours per week and isn't receiving benefits like Universal Credit in his own name.

**Important to note:** This eligibility will last for up to 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. If during this time he starts approved education or training, an apprenticeship, finds work of 24+ hours per week, or starts claiming certain benefits, you would need to report the change.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

All eligibility criteria are met.
